title: PRD: Fallback Confidence Service and Migration Playbook
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary
-------
This PRD describes the Fallback Confidence Service (FCS): a lightweight, low-latency classifier and scoring service that predicts the expected quality delta and operational risk of routing a request to a cheaper or higher‑latency model variant. The FCS is intended to power automated fallback decisions in the runtime, provide explainability signals to the Console, and enable a safe migration playbook for customers moving between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Goals
-----
- Provide a real-time confidence score (0.0–1.0) per request that estimates whether a fallback variant will meet tenant-defined quality bounds.
- Surface per-route and per-tenant historical fallback outcomes to Console and telemetry for auditing and billing.
- Enable an automated, reversible migration playbook for customers transitioning between model variants or deployment types with minimal regression risk.
- Keep inference latency impact <= 5 ms p50 when integrated into the fast path.

Non-goals
---------
- Replacing full model evaluation (shadowing/evals) for every regression check. FCS augments, not substitutes, robust offline evals.
- Supporting arbitrary third-party models in the initial rollout; launch supports Redwood-verified variants and marketplace-adapted adapters.

Product requirements (high level)
--------------------------------
| ID | Requirement | Rationale | Priority | Acceptance criteria |
|----|-------------|-----------|----------|---------------------|
| R-1 | Per-request confidence score API (float) | Drive routing decisions and analytics | P0 | API returns score within 0–1 and 95th percentile latency < 8ms under production load |
| R-2 | Per-route historic outcome stream (success/fallback/regression) | Auditable rollback and billing adjustments | P0 | Console shows aggregated fallback accuracy and daily regression counts |
| R-3 | Tenant policy DSL for fallbacks | Customers set allowable quality deltas and SLOs | P1 | Policies editable in Console; policy evaluation tests pass in sandbox |
| R-4 | Migration playbook templates (hosted↔dedicated↔private) | Reduce operational risk during migration | P1 | Step-by-step runbook with automated canary steps and rollback triggers |
| R-5 | Shadow mode and backtesting harness | Validate FCS decisions against offline evals | P0 | Shadow runs produce matching metrics with live traffic within tolerance |

API contract (example)
----------------------
Request (POST /v1/fcs/score):
```yaml
model_variant: "redwood-llm-ggml-compact-v1"
input_hash: "sha256:..."
prompt_features:
  - token_count: 38
  - contains_code: false
  - avg_sentence_length: 12.3
  - domain: "support-ticket"
tenant_id: "tenant-123"
route: "/chat/complete"
```
Response (200):
```json
{
  "score": 0.87,             // higher => safe to fallback
  "explanation": "prefix-match to high-confidence prompts; few OOV tokens",
  "model_compat": ["compact-v1", "compact-v1-quant"],
  "evaluation_ts": "2026-10-20T16:02:30Z"
}
```
Note: score interpretation is tenant-configurable (example: score>=0.8 allowed).

Policy DSL (concise)
--------------------
- allow_fallback_when: score >= 0.8
- max_quality_delta: 0.03 (relative likelihood of answer match)
- min_success_rate_last_24h: 0.985
- rollback_on: regression_count >= 3 in 1h

Telemetry and observability requirements
--------------------------------------
- Emit metrics per request: fcs.score (gauge), fcs.decision (enum: allow/deny), fcs.latency_ms (histogram).
- SLOs: FCS availability 99.99% monthly; false-allow rate <= 0.5% for P0 routes; processing p95 latency < 12ms.
- Traces: attach FCS decision as tag to request traces for per-request debug.
- Console: new FCS dashboard with per-tenant heatmaps (score distribution), rollback events, and a migration timeline view.

Migration playbook (high level)
------------------------------
1. Pre-migration validation (3–14 days):
   - Run FCS in shadow mode against intended fallback variant.
   - Collect shadow_metrics: "predicted_safe_rate", "observed_success_rate".
   - Required threshold: predicted_safe_rate >= 99% and observed_success_rate >= tenant_policy.min_success_rate_last_24h.
2. Canary (0.5–2% traffic):
   - Enable automated canary routing where FCS decides; monitor replay validation and user-facing errors.
   - Run for 4–24 hours depending on traffic volume.
3. Gradual ramp (2%→25%→50%→100%):
   - Ramp steps tied to time and explicit success gates (no regressions for 4 hours).
   - Automated rollback triggers on regression_count or drop in NPS for tenant.
4. Post-migration audit (7 days):
   - Run a full drift report comparing pre/post lexicon coverage, latency, and cost delta.
   - Create a migration summary for the customer and for internal SRE review.

Operational runbook (excerpt)
----------------------------
- P0: FCS returns malformed responses or causes routing errors:
  1. Switch runtime routing to "deny-by-default" (block fallback) using the feature toggle.
  2. Promote last known good FCS model via the model-store API.
  3. Notify oncall: eng-serving-runtime and product oncall.
- P1: Elevated false-allow rate (>0.5%):
  1. Throttle fallback decisions to shadow mode for affected route.
  2. Start capture: save last 10k affected request payloads for offline analysis.
  3. Trigger targeted retrain/eval in the lab.

Security and data handling
-------------------------
- Inputs to FCS must honor tenant privacy: no PII retention beyond 7 days in hot storage; all persisted features are hashed or token-count-only when possible.
- FCS runs in a tenant-scoped namespace; access controlled via RBAC and audit-logged.
- Any explainability artifacts stored with request traces are redacted for PII.

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
-----------------------------
- Functional: Per-request score available and evaluated by runtime for 99% of supported routes.
- Performance: End-to-end fallback decision adds <5ms p50 latency and <12ms p95 latency.
- Quality: False-allow rate <= 0.5% on P0 routes during 30-day canary window.
- Observability: Console displays historical accuracy and has filters by tenant/route/variant.

Rollout timeline (tentative)
---------------------------
- Q4 2026 (alpha): internal Redwood services and 3 pilot customers; shadow-only mode.
- Q1 2027 (beta): graduated pilot customers on hosted; Console integration for policies and dashboards.
- Q2 2027 (GA): Dedicated and Private onramp; migration playbook published and SRE playbooks finalized.

Risks and mitigations
---------------------
- Risk: FCS makes conservative decisions that reduce cost-savings.
  - Mitigation: Allow tenant-tunable sensitivity and post-migration cost-reconciliation credits.
- Risk: Latency regression on high-throughput routes.
  - Mitigation: Local caching and a lightweight feature extractor; fallback to precomputed scores for common prefixes.
- Risk: Explainability reveals sensitive prompts.
  - Mitigation: Redaction and hashed feature storage; privacy review for any explainability UI.

Related artifacts and references
-------------------------------

- Telemetry: consumption-telemetry-provenance-and-crediting-spec.
- Migration patterns: hosted-to-dedicated-transition-playbook.

Appendix: sample backtesting query
--------------------------------
- Query: compare FCS predicted_allow at T0 to observed success at T+24h for N=100k requests; compute confusion matrix and expected cost delta.
- Example SQL pseudocode:
  SELECT predicted_allow, observed_success, COUNT(*) FROM shadow_runs
  WHERE route = '/chat/complete' AND date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'
  GROUP BY predicted_allow, observed_success;

Next steps
----------
- Align product and serving-runtime on feature set and API latency budget (by 2026-10-27).
- Kickoff alpha integration with two internal services and identify 3 external pilot customers (by 2026-11-10).
- Draft Console policy editor mockups and telemetry dashboard wireframes (by 2026-11-03).
